subject: Urban Planning
title: School Streets: Safe Routes for Kids
description: A micro-lesson that makes School Streets: Safe Routes for Kids usable.

hook.text: London closes streets around 500 schools during drop-off and pick-up. No cars allowed. Kids own the road.

buildup.text: School streets ban motor traffic at set times. Bollards go up, children walk in, and air pollution drops instantly.

discovery.text: Pollution at school gates drops 23% on average. Children breathe cleaner air exactly when they need it most.

twist.text: Parents driving their kids to school create the very danger that makes other parents afraid to let kids walk.

climax.text: Barcelona, Edinburgh, and New York are expanding school street programs. The concept is spreading fast.

punchline.text: Close the road. Let the kids walk. The danger was us.

quiz.question: What happens to air pollution when school streets ban car traffic?
options: Pollution increases because cars idle on nearby streets instead
Pollution at school gates drops by an average of 23%
Pollution stays the same because most comes from distant sources
